header:
Date: 2026-04-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (Kyros CISO), Maya Singh (Kyros VP Eng), Omar Khalid (Kyros DevOps)
summary: Discovery-style security posture call. Kyros is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for PII-sensitive inference workloads. Main areas: SOC2/ISO status, SSO and RBAC, audit logging / log retention, encryption/KMS, data retention and deletion, and evidence for procurement. They requested docs and a pilot for performance and security validation.
topics: Encryption at rest / in transit, KMS/BYOK
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, I lead the enterprise AE motion. We have Priya and Jordan from our security/solutions team. Could we do quick intros?
[00:27] Daniel Ortiz: Hi, Daniel Ortiz, CISO at Kyros. We're looking at vendors to run model inference — need to understand security posture, compliance, and where we can place workloads.
[01:12] Maya Singh: Maya here, VP Eng. Focused on latency and cost but security is the blocker for procurement.
[02:05] Alex Kim: Great. Quick agenda — we'll cover our certifications, SSO and RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS, and deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private). Then Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[05:10] Priya Patel: To start, on certifications: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II — we will share the report — and we're in progress on ISO 27001, expected attestation this quarter. The hosted platform uses Redwood-managed keys by default; for enterprise customers we offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private via KMS/HSM integrations.
[08:00] Omar Khalid: Quick clarification: for hosted, do you support BYOK or HSM-backed keys?
[08:20] Priya Patel: Hosted by default is Redwood-managed KMS; we can do BYOK/HSM for hosted customers under an enterprise contract but most customers move to Dedicated or Private if they require full BYOK with on-prem HSMs. We'll put exact options in the doc.
[12:10] Daniel Ortiz: For auditability — do you provide immutable audit logs, and can we stream logs to our SIEM?
[12:35] Jordan Reyes: Yes, we provide per-tenant audit logs for auth events, API calls, and admin actions. Logs are accessible through the Console with export and can be pushed to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 export. We also keep an append-only audit store, and we can configure retention windows per contract.
[15:30] Maya Singh: How granular is RBAC? Can we map to groups from our SAML provider?
[15:48] Priya Patel: We integrate SSO via SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning — you can sync groups and map them to roles in Redwood. Roles are customizable: admin, dev, billing, auditor, etc. You can also create scoped API keys with least privilege.
[20:00] Daniel Ortiz: Data residency is important. We have EU PII that cannot leave region. What options do we have?
[20:20] Alex Kim: For data residency, Hosted has regional deployments — we can pin workloads to specific regions, but for strict legal residency or on-prem requirements Dedicated (customer-dedicated capacity in a region) or Private (VPC / on-prem install) are the recommended routes. Private supports air-gapped on-prem if needed.
[24:10] Omar Khalid: About data retention — do you retain customer logs or prompts by default? Can we opt out?
[24:35] Jordan Reyes: By default, we have short-lived logs for debugging and system metrics; customer prompt/response retention is configurable. For Hosted, standard retention is 30 days but we offer options to disable retention or shorten windows for compliance. Dedicated and Private give full control — you can disable storage of prompts, and logs can be forwarded to your storage.
[28:00] Maya Singh: Encryption at rest — do you support per-tenant encryption keys?
[28:20] Priya Patel: Yes. For Dedicated and Private you can use customer-managed KMS keys. Hosted supports per-customer key isolation with Redwood-managed keys and BYOK via enterprise add-on. All in-transit traffic is TLS 1.2+ with mutual TLS options for Private.
[32:10] Daniel Ortiz: We need to show procurement that you have third-party pen tests and vuln management.
[32:30] Jordan Reyes: We run regular internal and external pen tests, a vuln management program, and backlog tracking. We can provide penetration test summaries and SOC 2 evidence, and for deeper validators we can coordinate red-team engagements under NDA.
[36:00] Omar Khalid: Network layout for Dedicated — how does egress work, and can we route through our VPC?
[36:25] Priya Patel: Dedicated typically places GPU pools in a customer-isolated VPC in the cloud account or in Redwood-managed accounts with VPC peering options. We can support VPC peering, private endpoints, and NAT/egress control so you can lock down outbound traffic. We'll diagram that in the architecture doc.
[40:10] Maya Singh: What about secrets / key lifecycle — rotation, access controls?
[40:30] Alex Kim: We follow key rotation best practices; for customer-managed keys rotation is handled in your KMS. For Redwood-managed keys we rotate regularly and maintain KMS audit logs. Access to keys is strictly limited via RBAC and logged in the audit trail.
[44:00] Daniel Ortiz: Any known compliance gaps? Things you can't do in hosted vs private?
[44:20] Priya Patel: Short answer: Hosted is easiest for time-to-value, but dedicated/private are recommended when you need BYOK with HSM, air-gapped on-prem, or strict data residency guarantees and full control over retention. We'll call out the differences clearly in the follow-up.
[47:30] Alex Kim: Quick recap — we'll send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO status, an architecture diagram showing Hosted/Dedicated/Private flows, KMS/HSM options, and a pricing estimate. Priya will own the diagrams and the technical annex. Omar will share Kyros infra diagram. Any other asks?
[47:50] Daniel Ortiz: Please include evidence for pen tests and a sample AUP/BAA language. That would help procurement.
[48:00] Alex Kim: Got it — we'll include pen test summaries and BAA language. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items and schedule the pilot once Kyros shares the infra details.
